To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inclusion of CSM at the level of 30% in the diet of broiler chickens reduced the growth performance and dressing and breast percentage.
the addition of CSM in the diet at 20% level is better than 30% and that digestible lysine is not required in broiler chicken diet.

the addition of 0.8, 0.9 and 1.1% of digestible lysin did not improve the performance and carcass traits of broiler chickens fed on diets supplemented with 20% and30% CSM; and the enzyme supplementation did not show any improvement in the performance of birds fed CSM based diets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the effect of CSM and its supplementation of enzyme and digestible Lysine.
the evaluation of enzyme supplementation and digestible lysines in the diet of broilers fed on 30% CSE.
the effect of enzyme supplementation on the performance and carcass traits of broilers fed on CSM-supplemented diets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of 1.0 % digestible lysine and 30% CCM with the applicability to ideal protein concept and enzyme supplementation did not improve growth performance or carcass characteristics of broiler chickens.
the addition of CSM up to 30% in the diet of broiler chickens can be recommended with the application of enzyme and ideal protein concept.
the enzyme supplementation was not beneficial in improving the performance of broiler chickens fed on CSM-supplemented diets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
30% of CSM in the diet of broiler chickens can be used with the application of 1.0 % digestible lysine and enzyme supplementation.
the addition of 20% CSM in the diet is sufficient for the growth performance, carcass characteristics and immune response of broilers.

the addition of CSM in the broiler diet can improve the antibody titres against infectious diseases but the growth performance and the carcass characteristics were unaffected by the addition of CCM and supplemental enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CSM can be incorporated in broiler diets at 20% level without any adverse effect on performance and immune response.
the addition of CSM in the diet at 30% with 1.0 % digestible lysine and enzyme supplementation can be used as an alternative protein source without affecting the performance of broiler chicken.
the inclusion of CSM up to 20% is acceptable and the inclusion of 1.0%, digestible lysine is sufficient in broiler diets based on vegetable protein sources.
